academic_validation.independent_result: (A) on the negative direction of the x-axis

records.official_answer_locator: NCERT Exemplar Class IX Mathematics, Answers Unit 3, Ex 3.1 Q5

reasoning: Points on the x-axis have form (x,0). The abscissa is the first coordinate x, which may be any real number, while only the ordinate is fixed at zero.

records.official_answer_locator: NCERT Exemplar Class IX Mathematics, Answers Unit 3, Ex 3.1 Q6

reasoning: Every point on the x-axis has form (x,0), so its ordinate, the second coordinate, is always zero.

records.official_answer_locator: NCERT Exemplar Class IX Mathematics, Answers Unit 3, Ex 3.1 Q7

reasoning: The x-axis and y-axis intersect at the point (0,0). By definition, that intersection point is the origin.

records.official_answer_locator: NCERT Exemplar Class IX Mathematics, Answers Unit 3, Ex 3.1 Q8

reasoning: The third quadrant consists of points with both coordinates negative. Therefore a point with sign pattern (-,-) lies in quadrant III.

records.official_answer_text: (D) do not lie in the same quadrant
records.official_answer_locator: NCERT Exemplar Class IX Mathematics, Answers Unit 3, Ex 3.1 Q9

academic_validation.independent_result: (D) do not lie in the same quadrant
reasoning: The points (1,-1), (2,-2), and (4,-5) have sign pattern (+,-) and lie in quadrant IV. The point (-3,-4) has sign pattern (-,-) and lies in quadrant III, so the four points do not all lie in the same quadrant.

records.official_answer_locator: NCERT Exemplar Class IX Mathematics, Answers Unit 3, Ex 3.1 Q10

reasoning: If the y-coordinate is zero, the point has form (x,0). Every such point lies on the x-axis, including the origin when x=0.
